summary:
The legal position a trans visitor meets in Austria is broadly permissive. Sex between men was decriminalised in 1971, marriage has been open to same-sex couples since 2017, and full adoption rights have applied since 2016. A trans visitor travelling with a partner in what Austrian law would classify as a same-sex relationship therefore stands inside the ordinary marriage and family framework rather than outside it.

The Equal Treatment Act has prohibited employment discrimination on grounds of sexual orientation since 2004. Recent amendments broaden its use of "gender" to cover gender identity, gender expression and sex characteristics; gender identity and intersex status have no separate listing and are handled under that term. Since January 2017 every federal state has extended anti-discrimination protection to goods and services, Lower Austria being the last to do so, which places hotels, restaurants, shops and other commercial venues inside the regime.

Hate speech on grounds of sexual orientation has been prohibited since 1 January 2016, and an offence committed on that ground is treated as an aggravating factor at sentencing. The 1993 Security Police Act obliges officers to avoid actions perceived as biased on grounds of sexual orientation. No data on complaints against police or on disciplinary outcomes under that duty appears in the sources.

The serious documented risk is a coordinated ambush campaign. Police arrested 15 people, aged between 14 and 26, in March 2025. At least 17 people were lured through fake dating-platform accounts to remote locations, set upon by masked groups, filmed, and falsely accused of being paedophiles; investigators said the true number of victims was probably much higher. The network behind the attacks is described as neo-Nazi, and the recordings were circulated. The lures targeted men seeking men, so a trans man who uses such applications and is read as a man falls within the group the accounts were aimed at.

Police recorded 6,751 suspected hate crimes in 2025, logged 7,327 prejudice motives, and counted 1,575 people as victims of prejudice-related violence. These are raw counts and the police data are acknowledged to under-record. Within the same reporting year, offences classed as homophobic rose while transphobic incidents declined.

Official documents can carry an "X" marker or no gender entry, following the Constitutional Court's June 2018 ruling that gender identity must be accurately reflected in official records; the first such passport and a birth certificate marked "divers" went to an intersex applicant. Intersex people may also choose "diverse", "inter", or no designation. Legal gender recognition is described as available without mandatory medical procedures, although other accounts state that a change of legal gender or name is conditional on submitting a psychiatric opinion, and that the Interior Ministry restricted the "divers" designation to holders of a medical panel certificate of intersexuality.

The national ombuds institution has issued guidance on gender-inclusive administrative forms for intersex and non-binary people.

If a trans visitor is taken into custody, the Justice Ministry's answer to parliamentary question XXVIII. AB 774 of May and June 2025 sets out the official rules on housing transgender people in penal institutions. A 2025 national report by the Ludwig Boltzmann Institute, produced within a programme funded at European level, covers the legal framework governing LGBTIQ detainees, their situation and rights in detention, including gender self-determination and anti-discrimination protection.
tangentialFactors:
The Freedom Party (FPÖ) took 29.2 per cent in the September 2024 national election, the first time it had won the largest share of the vote since the Second World War; the ÖVP and FPÖ have historically opposed LGBT rights. Against that, openly LGBT politicians have held national office since 2019 and the federal president took part in the 2019 EuroPride parade in Vienna.

A petition for dedicated queer sauna time slots in Vienna was rejected, leaving no municipal provision of that kind in the capital. The Ministry of Education issued new rules restricting outside providers of sex education in schools.

Advocacy organisations operate openly, among them HOSI Wien (founded 1979), HOSI Salzburg, ALGF and Afro Rainbow Austria. Community infrastructure exists in Vienna, Linz, Innsbruck, Salzburg and Graz, and an annual Regenbogenparade is held in Vienna.
localsOnly:
Conversion therapy has no enacted statutory ban. The National Council passed a non-binding resolution on 2 July 2019 calling for a government bill prohibiting the practice on minors, with all parties supporting it at the final vote. In 2018 the association TeenSTAR was found running classes for minors that presented sexual orientation as changeable; the Education Directorate Salzburg banned its workshops pending review, the association was banned in April 2019, and the parliamentary resolution followed.

Legal gender change and name change do not require prior sex-reassignment surgery, but are conditional on submitting a psychiatric opinion. Public health insurance payment for sex-change treatment is likewise bound to the submission of psychiatric opinions.

Puberty blockers for adolescents experiencing gender dysphoria are endorsed by the Austrian Society of Child and Adolescent Psychiatry (ÖGKJP) and the Austrian Society of Gynecology and Obstetrics (OEGGG). Lesbian couples can access artificial insemination and IVF. Transgender people have been permitted to serve openly in the Austrian Armed Forces since 2014.
outOfScopeNotes:
The requirements attached to legal gender recognition are not settled in the sources. One account states that a change is possible without mandatory medical procedures; another states that a psychiatric opinion is required; a third reports that the Interior Ministry confined the "divers" designation to holders of a medical panel certificate of intersexuality. Whether the certificate requirement applies only to the third marker or also to binary changes is unresolved, and the sources do not establish whether an "X" marker is available to trans applicants who are not intersex.

The 2025 hate-crime figures are raw counts. The inventory carries no per-capita breakdown by victim group and no general homicide rate against which the trans-specific figures could be compared, so no magnitude of trans-specific risk can be calculated from them; the police data are additionally described as under-recorded.

No information on how the Security Police Act duty is enforced in practice, or on complaints and disciplinary outcomes, appears in the inventory.

The legal status of conversion therapy rests on a non-binding parliamentary resolution; no enacted prohibition is sourced, and the position after the review period is not established. On compensation for historical convictions, the only sourced statement is that no expungement or compensation scheme had been implemented as of July 2020; nothing later is available.
